CHAMP Jastrow Factor

1. Introduction

The Jastrow factor depends on the electronic (𝐫) and nuclear (𝐑) coordinates. It is defined as exp(J(𝐫,𝐑)), where

J(𝐫,𝐑)=JeN(𝐫,𝐑)+Jee(𝐫)+JeeN(𝐫,𝐑)

In the following, we use the notations rij=|𝐫i−𝐫j| and Riα=|𝐫i−𝐑α|.

JeN contains electron-nucleus terms:

JeN(𝐫,𝐑)=∑α=1Nnucl∑i=1Nelec(a1αfα(Riα)1+a2αfα(Riα)+∑p=2Nordaap+1α[fα(Riα)]p−JeN∞α)

Jee contains electron-electron terms:

Jee(𝐫)=∑i=1Nelec∑j=1i−1(12(1+δij↑↓)b1fee(rij)1+b2fee(rij)+∑p=2Nordbbp+1[fee(rij)]p)−Jee∞

and JeeN contains electron-electron-nucleus terms:

JeeN(𝐫,𝐑)=∑α=1Nnucl∑i=1Nelec∑j=1i−1∑p=2Nord∑k=0p−1∑l=0p−k−2δk,0clkpα[ge(rij)]k[[gα(Riα)]l+[gα(Rjα)]l][gα(Riα)gα(Rjα)](p−k−l)/2

clkpα are non-zero only when p−k−l is even.

The scaling functions f and g are defined as

fα(r)=1−e−καrκα and gα(r)=e−καr=1−καfα(r).

The terms Jee∞ and JeN∞ are shifts to ensure that Jee and JeN have an asymptotic value of zero.

The eN and eeN parameters are shared by all nuclei of the same type. Note that nucleus types are zero-based.

Derivatives are taken with respect to the coordinates of one electron, the other particles being fixed. For the electron-electron distance rij=|𝐫i−𝐫j| this gives ∇irij=−∇jrij.

Each of the three terms has its own set of routines, which deliver the value, the gradient and the Laplacian with respect to the electron coordinates, and the derivatives with respect to the parameters of the term. The last section combines them into the total Jastrow factor and its derivatives.

1.1. Reformulation of the three-body part

To accelerate the computation of the three-body part, the Jastrow factor is re-expressed as follows, with m=(p−k)/2−l/2:

Jkpl=∑α=1Nnucl∑i=1Nelec∑j=1i−1clkpα[ge(rij)]k[[gα(Riα)]l+[gα(Rjα)]l][gα(Riα)gα(Rjα)]m=12∑α=1Nnucl∑i=1Nelec∑j=1Nelecclkpα[ge(rij)]k[[gα(Riα)]l+[gα(Rjα)]l][gα(Riα)gα(Rjα)]m=12∑α=1Nnucl∑i=1Nelec∑j=1Nelecclkpα[ge(rij)]k[[gα(Riα)]l+m[gα(Rjα)]m+[gα(Riα)]l[gα(Rjα)]l+m]=∑α=1Nnuclclkpα∑i=1Nelec∑j=1Nelec[gα(Riα)]l+m[ge(rij)]k[gα(Rjα)]m=∑α=1Nnuclclkpα∑i=1Nelec[gα(Riα)]l+mPiαkm, with Piαkm=∑j=1Nelec[ge(rij)]k[gα(Rjα)]m.J=∑p=2Nord∑k=0p−1∑l=0p−k−2δk,0∑α=1Nnuclclkpα∑i=1Nelec[gα(Riα)](p−k+l)/2Piαk,(p−k−l)/2

The computation of P scales as 𝒪(Nelec2Nnucln2), and the computation of J scales as 𝒪(NelecNnucln2).

2.1. Data structure

The uninitialized integer contains one bit set to one for each initialization function which has not been called. It becomes equal to zero after all initialization functions have been called. The struct is then initialized and provided == true. Some values are initialized by default, and are not concerned by this mechanism.

2.2. Initialization functions

To prepare for the Jastrow and its derivative, all the following functions need to be called.

When the required information is completely entered, other data structures are computed to accelerate the calculations. The intermediates factors are precontracted using BLAS LEVEL 3 operations.

2.3.0.1. Fortran interface

3. Computation

The computed data is stored in the context so that it can be reused by different kernels. To ensure that the data is valid, for each computed data the date of the context is stored when it is computed. To know if some data needs to be recomputed, we check if the date of the dependencies are more recent than the date of the data to compute. If it is the case, then the data is recomputed and the current date is stored.

3.1. Electron-electron component

3.1.1. Asymptotic component

Calculate the asymptotic component asymp_jasb to be subtracted from the electron-electron jastrow factor Jee. Two values are computed. The first one is for parallel spin pairs, and the second one for antiparallel spin pairs. If the spin_independent variable is set to 1, then δ↑↓ is always equal to one.

Jee∞=12(1+δ↑↓)b1κee−11+b2κee−1+∑p=2Nordbbp+1κee−p

3.1.1.2. Compute

b_vector double[bord_num+1] in Values of b
rescale_factor_ee double in Factor to rescale ee distances
spin_independent int32_t in If 1, use the same parameters for parallel and antiparallel spin pairs
asymp_jasb double[2] out Asymptotic values for parallel and antiparallel spin pairs

3.1.2. Electron-electron rescaled distances

ee_distance_rescaled stores the matrix of the rescaled distances between all pairs of electrons:

Cij=1−e−κrijκ

where rij is the matrix of electron-electron distances.

3.1.2.1. Get
3.1.2.2. Compute
Variable Type In/Out Description
context qmckl_context in Global state
elec_num int64_t in Number of electrons
rescale_factor_ee double in Factor to rescale ee distances
walk_num int64_t in Number of walkers
coord double[3][walk_num][elec_num] in Electron coordinates
ee_distance double[walk_num][elec_num][elec_num] out Electron-electron rescaled distances

3.1.3. Electron-electron rescaled distance gradients and Laplacian with respect to electron coordinates

The rescaled distances, represented by Cij=(1−e−κerij)/κe are differentiated with respect to the electron coordinates. This information is stored in the tensor ee_distance_rescaled_gl. The initial three sequential elements of this three-dimensional tensor provide the x, y, and z direction derivatives, while the fourth index corresponds to the Laplacian.

3.1.3.1. Get
3.1.3.2. Compute
Variable Type In/Out Description
context qmckl_context in Global state
elec_num int64_t in Number of electrons
rescale_factor_ee double in Factor to rescale ee distances
walk_num int64_t in Number of walkers
coord double[3][walk_num][elec_num] in Electron coordinates
ee_distance_rescaled_gl double[walk_num][elec_num][elec_num][4] out Electron-electron rescaled distance derivatives

3.1.4. Electron-electron component

Calculate the electron-electron jastrow component factor_ee using the asymp_jasb component and the electron-electron rescaled distances ee_distance_rescaled. If the spin_independent variable is set to 1, then δ↑↓ is always equal to one.

fee=∑i,j<i[12(1+δij↑↓)B0Cij1+B1Cij+∑k=2NordbBkCijk−Jee∞ij]

δ is the spin factor, B is the vector of b parameters, C is the array of rescaled distances.

fee can be rewritten as:

fee=12[∑i,j12(1+δij↑↓)B0Cij1+B1Cij+∑i,j∑k=2NordbBkCijk]−[n↑(n↑−1)+n↓(n↓−1)2Jee∞↑↑+n↑n↓Jee∞↑↓]

3.1.4.1. Get
  1. Fortran interface
3.1.4.2. Compute
Variable Type In/Out Description
context qmckl_context in Global state
walk_num int64_t in Number of walkers
elec_num int64_t in Number of electrons
up_num int64_t in Number of alpha electrons
bord_num int64_t in Number of b coefficients
b_vector double[bord_num+1] in Values of b
ee_distance_rescaled double[walk_num][elec_num][elec_num] in Rescaled electron-electron distances
asymp_jasb double[2] in Asymptotic values subtracted from the electron-electron term
factor_ee double[walk_num] out fee

3.1.5. Derivative

The derivative of factor_ee is computed using the ee_distance_rescaled and the electron-electron rescaled distances derivatives ee_distance_rescaled_gl. There are four components, the gradient which has 3 components in the x,y,z directions and the laplacian as the last component.

∇ifee=∑j≠i[12(1+δij↑↓)B0∇iCij(1+B1Cij)2+∑k=2NordbBkkCijk−1∇iCij]

Δifee=∑j≠i[12(1+δij↑↓)B0(ΔiCij(1+B1Cij)2−2B1(∇iCij)2(1+B1Cij)3)+∑k=2NordbBkk((k−1)Cijk−2(∇iCij)2+Cijk−1ΔiCij)]

3.1.5.2. Compute

3.1.6. Parameter Derivative of the Asymptotic component

Calculate the derivatives of the asymptotic component w.r.t. the jastrow parameters asymp_jasb_pderiv to be subtracted from the electron-electron jastrow factor Jee derivatives. Two values are computed. The first one is for parallel spin pairs, and the second one for antiparallel spin pairs. If the spin_independent variable is set to 1, then δ↑↓ is always equal to one.

Jee∞=12(1+δ↑↓)B0κee−11+B1κee−1+∑p=2NordbBp+1κee−p

∂B0Jee∞=12(1+δij↑↓)κee−11+B1κee−1

∂B1Jee∞=−12(1+δij↑↓)κee−2(1+B1κee−1)2

∂BkJee∞=κee−(k−1)
for k>1

3.1.6.2. Compute

bord_num int64_t in Order of the b polynomial
b_vector double[bord_num+1] in Values of b
rescale_factor_ee double in Factor to rescale ee distances

asymp_jasb_pderiv double[2][bord_num+1] out Parameter derivatives of the electron-electron asymptotic values

3.1.7. Parameter Derivative

The derivative of factor_ee with respect to the jastrow parameters b_vector is computed. These derivatives are computed from the electron-electron rescaled distances ee_distance_rescaled and the parameter derivatives of the asymptotic part asymp_jasb_pderiv. If spin_independent is set to 1, then δ↑↓ is always equal to 1. Cij is the rescaled distance ee_distance_rescaled, not the bare distance rij.

&part;<sub>B<sub>0</sub></sub>f<sub></sub>ee=&sum;<sub>j=1</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>elec</sup>&sum;<sub>i=1</sub><sup>j−1</sup>[12(1+&delta;<sup>&uarr;&darr;</sup><sub>ij</sub>)C<sub>ij</sub>1+B<sub>1</sub>C<sub>ij</sub></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>&part;<sub>B<sub>0</sub></sub>J<sub>ee</sub><sup>&infin;</sup>]</li></ul><p>

∂B1fee=∑j=1Nelec∑i=1j−1[−12(1+δij↑↓)B0Cij2(1+B1Cij)2−∂B1Jee∞]

∂Bkfee=∑j=1Nelec∑i=1j−1[Cijk−∂BkJee∞]fork>1

The pair sums are accumulated over all walkers and divided by the number of walkers.

3.1.8. Parameter Derivative of the gradient and Laplacian

The derivatives of the gradient and Laplacian of factor_ee_gl with respect to the b coefficients are stored in factor_ee_gl_pderiv, with the parameter index first, then the electron index, and last the four coordinate components (x, y, z, Laplacian). The pair weight wij=12(1+δij↑↓) is used for the B0 and B1 derivatives, so that parallel pairs count half when spin_independent is zero. Writing Gij=(∇iCij)2:

∂B0∇ifee=∑j≠iwij∇iCij(1+B1Cij)2

&part;<sub>B<sub>0</sub></sub>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>f<sub></sub>ee=&sum;<sub>j&ne;i</sub>w<sub>ij</sub>[&Delta;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>ij</sub>(1+B<sub>1</sub>C<sub>ij</sub>)<sup>2</sup></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>2B<sub>1</sub>G<sub>ij</sub>(1+B<sub>1</sub>C<sub>ij</sub>)<sup>3</sup>]</li></ul><p>

∂B1∇ifee=−∑j≠i2B0wijCij∇iCij(1+B1Cij)3

&part;<sub>B<sub>1</sub></sub>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>f<sub></sub>ee=−&sum;<sub>j&ne;i</sub>2B<sub>0</sub>w<sub>ij</sub>(1+B<sub>1</sub>C<sub>ij</sub>)<sup>2</sup>[C<sub>ij</sub>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>ij</sub>1+B<sub>1</sub>C<sub>ij</sub></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>(1−2B<sub>1</sub>C<sub>ij</sub>)G<sub>ij</sub>(1+B<sub>1</sub>C<sub>ij</sub>)<sup>2</sup>]</li></ul><p>

&part;<sub>B<sub>k</sub></sub>&nabla;<sub>i</sub>f<sub></sub>ee=&sum;<sub>j&ne;i</sub>kC<sub>ij</sub><sup>k−1</sup>&nabla;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>ij</sub>,&part;<sub>B<sub>k</sub></sub>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>f<sub></sub>ee=&sum;<sub>j&ne;i</sub>k[C<sub>ij</sub><sup>k−1</sup>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>ij</sub></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>(k−1)C<sub>ij</sub><sup>k−2</sup>G<sub>ij</sub>]</li></ul><p>fork&gt;1

The sums run over all walkers and are divided by walk_num. Note that in qmckl_compute_jastrow_champ_factor_ee_gl_pderiv the Laplacian entry of ∂B0 is accumulated with the sign of its second term inverted.

3.2. Electron-nucleus component

3.2.1. Asymptotic component

Calculate the asymptotic component asymp_jasa to be subtracted from the final electron-nucleus jastrow factor JeN. The asymptotic component is calculated via the a_vector and the electron-nucleus rescale factors rescale_factor_en:

J<sub>eN</sub><sup>&infin;&alpha;</sup>=a<sub>1&alpha;</sub>&kappa;<sub>&alpha;</sub><sup>−1</sup>1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>&kappa;<sub>&alpha;</sub><sup>−1</sup></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>&sum;<sub>p=2</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>ord<sup>a</sup></sup>a<sub>p+1,&alpha;</sub>&kappa;<sub>&alpha;</sub><sup>−p</sup></li></ul><p>

where κα is the value of rescale_factor_en for the nucleus type α.

Ciα=1−e−καRiακα

where Riα is the matrix of electron-nucleus distances.

3.2.3. Electron-nucleus rescaled distance gradients and Laplacian with respect to electron coordinates

The rescaled distances, represented by Ciα=(1−e−καRiα)/κα are differentiated with respect to the electron coordinates. This information is stored in the tensor en_distance_rescaled_gl. The initial three sequential elements of this three-index tensor provide the x, y, and z direction derivatives, while the fourth index corresponds to the Laplacian.

3.2.5. Derivative

The derivative of the electron-nucleus jastrow component factor_en_gl with respect to the electron coordinates is calculated in the function qmckl_compute_jastrow_champ_factor_en_gl, using the en_distance_rescaled and en_distance_rescaled_gl arrays which are already calculated previously. Writing Ciα for the rescaled distance between electron i and nucleus α, the gradient is:

&nabla;<sub>i</sub>f<sub></sub>eN=&sum;<sub>&alpha;=1</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>nucl</sup>[a<sub>1&alpha;</sub>&nabla;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub>(1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub>)<sup>2</sup></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>&sum;<sub>p=2</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>ord<sup>a</sup></sup>a<sub>p+1,&alpha;</sub>p</li></ul><p>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub><sup>p−1</sup>&nabla;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub>]

and the Laplacian is:

&Delta;<sub>i</sub>f<sub></sub>eN=&sum;<sub>&alpha;=1</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>nucl</sup>[a<sub>1&alpha;</sub>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub>(1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub>)<sup>2</sup></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>2a<sub>1&alpha;</sub>a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>(&nabla;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub>)<sup>2</sup></li></ul><p>(1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub>)<sup>3</sup></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>&sum;<sub>p=2</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>ord<sup>a</sup></sup>a<sub>p+1,&alpha;</sub></li></ul><p>(pC<sub>i&alpha;</sub><sup>p−1</sup>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>p(p−1)C<sub>i&alpha;</sub><sup>p−2</sup>(&nabla;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>i&alpha;</sub>)<sup>2</sup>)]</li></ul><p>

3.2.6. Parameter Derivative of the Asymptotic component

The derivatives of the asymptotic component asymp_jasa with respect to the parameters a_vector are stored in asymp_jasa_pderiv. They are computed from the a_vector and the electron-nucleus rescale factors rescale_factor_en. For each nucleus type α:

∂JeN∞α∂a1α=κα−11+a2ακα−1

∂JeN∞α∂a2α=−a1ακα−2(1+a2ακα−1)2

∂JeN∞α∂ap+1,α=κα−pforp≥2

3.2.7. Parameter Derivative

The parameter derivatives of the electron-nucleus jastrow component factor_en are stored in factor_en_pderiv. They are computed from the a_vector coefficients and the electron-nucleus rescaled distances en_distance_rescaled. Writing Ciβ for the rescaled distance between electron i and nucleus β, and α for the nucleus type:

&part;f<sub></sub>eN&part;a<sub>1&alpha;</sub>=&sum;<sub>&beta;</sub>&sum;<sub>i=1</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>elec</sup>[C<sub>i&beta;</sub>1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>i&beta;</sub></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>&part;J<sub>eN</sub><sup>&infin;&alpha;</sup>&part;a<sub>1&alpha;</sub>]</li></ul><p>

&part;f<sub></sub>eN&part;a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>=&sum;<sub>&beta;</sub>&sum;<sub>i=1</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>elec</sup>[−a<sub>1&alpha;</sub>C<sub>i&beta;</sub><sup>2</sup>(1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>i&beta;</sub>)<sup>2</sup></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>&part;J<sub>eN</sub><sup>&infin;&alpha;</sup>&part;a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>]</li></ul><p>

&part;f<sub></sub>eN&part;a<sub>p+1,&alpha;</sub>=&sum;<sub>&beta;</sub>&sum;<sub>i=1</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>elec</sup>[C<sub>i&beta;</sub><sup>p</sup></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>&part;J<sub>eN</sub><sup>&infin;&alpha;</sup>&part;a<sub>p+1,&alpha;</sub>]</li></ul><p>forp&ge;2

In these expressions β runs only over the nuclei of type α. The result is accumulated over the walkers and divided by the number of walkers.

The derivatives of the gradient and Laplacian of factor_en_gl with respect to the a coefficients are stored in factor_en_gl_pderiv, with the nucleus type first, then the parameter index, the electron index, and last the four coordinate components (x, y, z, Laplacian). Writing Cia for the rescaled distance between electron i and nucleus a, and Gia=(∇iCia)2, the sums run over the electrons and over the nuclei a of type α:

&part;<sub>a<sub>1&alpha;</sub></sub>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>f<sub></sub>eN=&sum;<sub>a&isin;&alpha;</sub>&sum;<sub>i=1</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>elec</sup>[&Delta;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>ia</sub>(1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>ia</sub>)<sup>2</sup></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>2a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>G<sub>ia</sub>(1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>ia</sub>)<sup>3</sup>]</li></ul><p>

&part;<sub>a<sub>2&alpha;</sub></sub>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>f<sub></sub>eN=−&sum;<sub>a&isin;&alpha;</sub>&sum;<sub>i=1</sub><sup>N<sub></sub>elec</sup>2a<sub>1&alpha;</sub>(1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>ia</sub>)<sup>3</sup>[C<sub>ia</sub>&Delta;<sub>i</sub>C<sub>ia</sub></p><ulclass="org−ul"><li>(1−2a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>ia</sub>)G<sub>ia</sub></li></ul><p>1+a<sub>2&alpha;</sub>C<sub>ia</sub>]

∂ap+1,α∇ifeN=∑a∈α∑i=1NelecpCiap−1∇iCia

∂ap+1,αΔifeN=∑a∈α∑i=1Nelecp[Ciap−1ΔiCia+(p−1)Ciap−2Gia]forp≥2

The sums run over all walkers and are divided by walk_num.

3.4.2. Derivatives

Gradients and Laplacian of the total Jastrow factor:

∇[eJ(𝐫)]=eJ(𝐫)∇J(𝐫)
Δ[eJ(𝐫)]=eJ(𝐫)[ΔJ(𝐫)+∇J(𝐫)·∇J(𝐫)]
